verses.text: So, a bunch of people have already tried to put together a solid account of everything God has brought about among us. 📜
They passed it down straight from the start—from the eyewitnesses who saw it all and served the message, the OGs who knew the story firsthand.
I traced everything carefully from the beginning too, most excellent Theophilus, and decided to write it all out for you in order, my dude.
That way, you can know for sure the teaching you received is legit. No guesswork. ✅
Back when Herod was king of Judea, there was a priest named Zacharias from Abijah’s division. His wife Elizabeth came from Aaron’s priestly family.
They both lived right before God, following the Lord’s commands faithfully—no fake show.
They had no child, because Elizabeth couldn’t have children, and both of them were getting up there in age. ⏳
One day Zacharias was doing his priestly service before God while his division was on duty.
The priestly custom used lots to choose who would enter the Lord’s sanctuary and burn incense. That turn landed on Zacharias.
The whole crowd outside was praying while the incense was being offered. 🙏
Then an angel of the Lord appeared, standing on the right side of the incense altar.
Zacharias froze when he saw him, and fear hit him hard.
But the angel said, “Don’t be afraid, Zacharias. Your prayer has been heard. Elizabeth, your wife, will have a son, and you’ll name him John. 👶”
“You’ll be full of joy, and many people will celebrate his birth. 🎉”
“He’ll be great in the Lord’s sight. He mustn’t drink wine or strong drink, and the Holy Spirit will fill him even before he’s born.”
“He’ll turn many people in Israel back to the Lord their God.”

“He’ll go ahead of the Lord with Elijah’s spirit and power, turning parents’ hearts toward their children and the disobedient toward the wisdom of the righteous. He’ll get a people ready for the Lord.” 📣
Zacharias said to the angel, “How can I know this is for real? I’m old, and my wife’s getting up there too.”
The angel answered, “I’m Gabriel. I stand in God’s presence, and I was sent to speak to you and bring you this good news.”
“Now listen: you’ll be unable to speak until this happens, because you didn’t believe my words. They’ll come true right on time.” 🤐
The people were waiting for Zacharias and wondered why he was taking so long in the sanctuary.
When he came out, he couldn’t speak to them. They realized he’d seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs, and stayed mute.
When his priestly service was done, Zacharias went back home.
After that, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant. She kept to herself for five months and said:
“The Lord has done this for me. He showed me kindness and took away the shame I carried among people.” 💛
In Elizabeth’s sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent by God to Nazareth, a town in Galilee.
He came to a virgin engaged to a man named Joseph, from David’s family. The virgin’s name was Mary.
The angel came in and said, “Rejoice, favored one! The Lord is with you. You’re blessed among women!”
Mary was seriously unsettled by what he said and wondered what kind of greeting this was.
The angel told her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary. God has shown you favor.”
“You’ll become pregnant and give birth to a son. Name him Jesus.”
“He’ll be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.”
“He’ll reign over Jacob’s family forever, and his Kingdom will never end.” 👑
Mary asked the angel, “How can this happen, since I’m a virgin?”
The angel answered, “The Holy Spirit will come over you, and the Most High’s power will cover you. So the holy child born to you will be called the Son of God.”
“And look—your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. She’s in her sixth month, though people called her unable to have children.”
“Nothing God says is impossible.”
Mary said, “I’m the Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me just as you’ve said.” Then the angel left her.
Mary got up in those days and hurried into the hill country, to a town in Judea.
She went into Zacharias’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby jumped inside her. Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit
and called out loudly, “You’re blessed among women, and blessed is the child you’re carrying!”
“How did I get this honor—that my Lord’s mother came to visit me?”
“The second your greeting reached my ears, the baby inside me jumped for joy!”
“You’re blessed because you believed the Lord would make good on what he told you!” 🙌
Mary said, “My whole being magnifies the Lord.”
“My spirit is celebrating God my Savior,”
“because he noticed his servant’s humble situation. From now on, every generation will call me blessed.”
“The Mighty One has done great things for me. His name is holy.”
“His mercy keeps reaching generation after generation of those who honor him.”
“He has flexed his strength and scattered the proud—the ones plotting big things in their hearts.”
“He has brought rulers down from their thrones and lifted up the humble.”
“He has filled hungry people with good things and sent rich people away empty.”
“He has helped Israel, his servant, remembering his mercy,”
“just as he promised our ancestors, Abraham and his descendants, forever.” ✨
Mary stayed with Elizabeth about three months, then went back home.
When Elizabeth’s time came, she gave birth to a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard how generously the Lord had shown her mercy, and they celebrated with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the baby. They planned to name him Zacharias, after his father.
But his mother said, “No way. He’ll be called John.”
They told her, “Nobody in your family has that name.”
They made signs to his father to ask what name he wanted.
Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” Everyone was amazed.
At once his mouth opened and his tongue was free. He began praising God. 🙌
Awe came over everyone living nearby, and people talked about all this throughout Judea’s hill country.
Everyone who heard kept thinking, “What will this child become?” The Lord’s hand was with him.
Zacharias, his father, was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied:
“Blessed is the Lord, Israel’s God! He has come to help and redeem his people.”
“He has raised up a powerful Savior for us from the family of his servant David,”
“just as he promised through his holy prophets long ago:”
“‘He’ll save us from our enemies and from everyone who hates us.”
“‘He’ll show mercy to our ancestors and remember his holy covenant,”
“‘the oath he swore to Abraham our ancestor:”
“‘He has rescued us from our enemies’ grip so we can serve him without fear,”
“‘living holy and upright before him all our days.”
“‘And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High. You’ll go ahead of the Lord and prepare his way,”
“‘showing his people how salvation comes through the forgiveness of their sins,”
“‘because our God is tender and full of mercy. Dawn from heaven is about to break over us,”
“‘shining on people sitting in darkness and under death’s shadow, guiding our feet onto the road of peace.’” 🕊️
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the wilderness until the day he appeared publicly to Israel. 🌱
In those days, Caesar Augustus issued an order: everybody across the empire had to get registered.
This was the first registration, while Quirinius was governing Syria.
Everyone went to register, each person heading to their own town.
Joseph went too, traveling up from Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to David’s town, Bethlehem. He belonged to David’s family line,
and went to register with Mary, who was engaged to him and was pregnant.
While they were there, the time came for Mary to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in cloths, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no space for them in the guest room. 👶
Nearby, shepherds were staying out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock at night.
Suddenly, an angel of the Lord stood near them, and the Lord’s glory shone all around. They were terrified.
The angel said, “Don’t be afraid! Look, I’m bringing you good news that will make everyone very happy.”
“Today, in David’s town, a Savior has been born for you. He is Christ the Lord.”
“Here’s your sign: you’ll find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a feeding trough.”
All at once, a huge heavenly army appeared with the angel, praising God and saying:
“Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to the people he favors!” 🌟
When the angels went back into heaven, the shepherds said to each other, “Let’s go straight to Bethlehem and see what happened—the Lord has let us know about it.”
They hurried there and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough.
After seeing him, they spread the word about what they’d been told about this child.
Everyone who heard the shepherds’ story was amazed at what they said.
Mary held onto all these words and kept turning them over in her heart.
The shepherds went back, praising and glorifying God for everything they’d heard and seen. It all happened just as they’d been told. 🙌
When the baby was eight days old and it was time to circumcise him, they named him Jesus—the name the angel had given before he was conceived.
When the time came for their purification under Moses’ Law, they brought Jesus to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
as the Lord’s Law says: “Every firstborn boy must be called holy to the Lord.”
They also came to offer the sacrifice required by the Lord’s Law: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was righteous and devoted, waiting for Israel’s consolation, and the Holy Spirit was with him.
The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he wouldn’t die before seeing the Lord’s Christ.
Guided by the Spirit, Simeon came into the temple. When Jesus’ parents brought the child in to do what the Law required,
Simeon took Jesus in his arms and praised God, saying:
“Master, now you can let your servant go in peace, just as you promised.”
“My eyes have seen your salvation,”
“which you prepared for all peoples to see—”
“a light to reveal you to the nations and the glory of your people Israel.” ✨
Joseph and Jesus’ mother were amazed at what people were saying about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, “This child is appointed to bring many in Israel down and raise many up. He’ll be a sign people speak against.”
“And a sword will pierce your own soul too, so the thoughts in many hearts can be revealed.”
There was also a prophet named Anna, daughter of Phanuel, from Asher’s tribe. She was very old: after marrying as a virgin, she had lived with her husband for seven years,
then had been a widow for about eighty-four years. She never left the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day.
Coming up at that very moment, Anna thanked the Lord and spoke about Jesus to everyone waiting for Jerusalem’s redemption.
When they had done everything required by the Lord’s Law, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom. God’s grace rested on him. 🌱
Every year Jesus’ parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover festival.
When Jesus was twelve, they went up to Jerusalem for the festival, as they usually did.
When the festival days were over and they started home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t realize it.
They assumed he was somewhere in the traveling group and went a whole day before looking for him among their relatives and friends.
When they couldn’t find him, they went back to Jerusalem searching for him.
After three days, they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at how much he understood and at his answers.
When his parents saw him, they were stunned. His mother said, “Son, why did you do this to us? Your father and I have been anxiously looking everywhere for you.”
He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?”
They didn’t understand what he meant by that.
Jesus went back with them to Nazareth and was obedient to them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
Jesus kept growing in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and people.
In Tiberius Caesar’s fifteenth year as emperor—while Pontius Pilate governed Judea, Herod ruled Galilee, his brother Philip ruled Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ruled Abilene—
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, God’s message came to Zacharias’s son John out in the wilderness.
John traveled all around the Jordan, preaching a baptism that showed people were turning back to God so their sins could be forgiven. 🌊
This is what Isaiah the prophet wrote: “A voice is calling out in the wilderness: ‘Get the Lord’s road ready; make his paths straight.”
“‘Every valley will be filled, every mountain and hill brought low. Crooked roads will become straight, and rough roads smooth.”
“‘Then everyone will see God’s salvation.’”
John told the crowds coming out to be baptized, “You bunch of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming judgment?”
“Live in a way that shows you’ve truly turned back to God. And don’t start saying, ‘Abraham is our father.’ I’m telling you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones!”
“Even now the axe is already at the trees’ roots. Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit gets cut down and thrown into the fire.” 🔥
The crowds asked him, “So what should we do?”
He answered, “If you have two coats, share one with someone who has none. If you have food, do the same.”
Tax collectors came to be baptized too. They asked him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He told them, “Don’t collect more than the amount you’re authorized to take.”
Some soldiers asked, “What about us? What should we do?” He said, “Don’t shake anyone down or accuse anyone falsely. Be satisfied with your pay.”
The people were full of expectation. Everyone was wondering privately whether John might be the Christ.
John answered them all, “I baptize you with water, but someone stronger than me is coming. I’m not worthy to loosen his sandal strap. He’ll baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.”
“His winnowing fork is in his hand. He’ll clear out his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with fire that can’t be put out.”
John used many other strong appeals to encourage the people and share the good news with them.
But John also called out Herod the ruler for marrying Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things he had done.
Herod added one more evil to the list: he locked John up in prison.
When all the people had been baptized, Jesus was baptized too. As he was praying, heaven opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down on him in a bodily form, like a dove. A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son. I’m pleased with you.” 🕊️
Jesus was about thirty when he began his work. People assumed he was Joseph’s son; Joseph was Heli’s son.
Heli’s line ran through Matthat, Levi, Melchi, Jannai, and Joseph.
Then came Mattathias, Amos, Nahum, Esli, and Naggai.
Then Maath, Mattathias, Semein, Joseph, and Judah.
Then Joanan, Rhesa, Zerubbabel, Shealtiel, and Neri.
Then Melchi, Addi, Cosam, Elmodam, and Er.
Then Jose, Eliezer, Jorim, Matthat, and Levi.
Then Simeon, Judah, Joseph, Jonan, and Eliakim.
Then Melea, Menan, Mattatha, Nathan, and David.
Then Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, and Nahshon.
Then Amminadab, Aram, Hezron, Perez, and Judah.
Then Jacob, Isaac, Abraham, Terah, and Nahor.
Then Serug, Reu, Peleg, Eber, and Shelah.
Then Cainan, Arphaxad, Shem, Noah, and Lamech.
Then Methuselah, Enoch, Jared, Mahalaleel, and Cainan.
Then Enos, Seth, Adam—and ultimately God.
Jesus, filled with the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan. The Spirit led him into the wilderness,
where the devil tested him for forty days. He ate nothing the whole time, and afterward he was hungry.
The devil said, “If you’re God’s Son, tell this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answered, “Scripture says, ‘A person doesn’t live on bread alone, but on every word from God.’”
The devil led Jesus up a high mountain and, in a flash, showed him every kingdom in the world.
The devil said, “I’ll give you all this authority and glory. It’s been handed over to me, and I can give it to anyone I want.”
“So if you worship me, it’ll all be yours.”
Jesus answered, “Get behind me, Satan! Scripture says, ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve only him.’”
Then the devil led him to Jerusalem, set him on the highest point of the temple, and said, “If you’re God’s Son, throw yourself down from here.”
“Because Scripture says, ‘He’ll order his angels to guard you,’”
“and, ‘They’ll carry you in their hands so you don’t hit your foot on a stone.’”
Jesus answered, “Scripture also says, ‘Don’t test the Lord your God.’”
When the devil had tried every temptation, he left Jesus until another opportunity came.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the Spirit’s power. News about him spread through the whole region.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
Jesus came to Nazareth, where he had grown up. On the Sabbath, as usual, he went into the synagogue and stood up to read.
They handed him the scroll of the prophet Isaiah. He opened it and found the passage that said:

“The Lord’s Spirit is on me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He sent me to heal the brokenhearted, announce freedom for prisoners, restore sight to the blind, and set oppressed people free,”
“and to announce the Lord’s year of favor.”
Jesus rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. Everyone in the synagogue was staring at him.
He began by telling them, “Today, as you’re hearing it, this Scripture has come true.”
Everyone spoke well of him and was amazed by the gracious words coming from him. But they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
Jesus said, “I know you’ll quote this saying to me: ‘Doctor, heal yourself!’ You’ll say, ‘Do here in your hometown what we heard you did in Capernaum.’”
He continued, “I’m telling you the truth: no prophet gets accepted in his hometown.”
“Think about it: there were many widows in Israel during Elijah’s time, when the sky stayed shut for three years and six months and a severe famine hit the whole land.”
“But Elijah wasn’t sent to any of them. He was sent to a widow in Zarephath, in Sidon’s territory.”
“And there were many people with skin diseases in Israel during Elisha the prophet’s time, but none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”
Everyone in the synagogue got furious when they heard this.
They jumped up, threw Jesus out of town, and took him to the edge of the hill their town was built on, planning to throw him off the cliff.
But Jesus walked right through the middle of them and went on his way.
Jesus went down to Capernaum, a city in Galilee, and taught the people on the Sabbath.
They were amazed at his teaching because his message carried authority.
In the synagogue there was a man controlled by an unclean demon. He shouted loudly:
“Hey! What do you want with us, Jesus from Nazareth? Did you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus ordered him, “Be quiet and come out of him!” The demon threw the man down in front of everyone, then came out without hurting him.
Everyone was stunned and said to each other, “What kind of message is this? He commands unclean spirits with authority and power, and they come out!”
News about Jesus spread everywhere in the surrounding region.
Jesus left the synagogue and went to Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they asked Jesus to help her.
He stood over her and ordered the fever to leave. It left her, and she immediately got up and served them.
At sunset, people brought him everyone who was sick with all kinds of diseases. Jesus laid his hands on each one and healed them.
Demons came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” Jesus rebuked them and wouldn’t let them speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
At daybreak, Jesus left and went to a deserted place. The crowds searched for him, found him, and tried to keep him from leaving.
But he told them, “I must announce the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other towns too. That’s why I was sent.”
So he kept preaching in the synagogues throughout Galilee.
A crowd was pressing in on Jesus to hear God’s message. He was standing by Lake Gennesaret.
He saw two boats at the lake’s edge. The fishermen had climbed out and were washing their nets.
Jesus got into Simon’s boat and asked him to push out a little from shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
When he finished teaching, he told Simon, “Head out to deeper water and lower your nets for a catch.”
Simon answered, “Boss, we worked all night and caught nothing. But since you say so, I’ll drop the nets again.”
They did, and caught so many fish that their nets started tearing. 🐟
They waved to their partners in the other boat to come help. The partners came, and they filled both boats so full they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell at Jesus’ knees and said, “Move away from me, Lord. I’m a sinful man.”
He and everyone with him were stunned by the huge catch they’d hauled in.
James and John, Zebedee’s sons and Simon’s partners, were just as amazed. Jesus told Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on, you’ll be catching people alive.”
They brought the boats to shore, left everything behind, and followed Jesus.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man covered with leprosy saw him. He fell facedown and begged, “Lord, if you’re willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus reached out, touched him, and said, “I am willing. Be clean!” Immediately the leprosy left him.
Jesus ordered him, “Don’t tell anyone. Go show yourself to the priest and bring the offering Moses commanded for your cleansing. Let that be your public proof.”
But reports about Jesus spread even more. Huge crowds came to hear him and be healed from their illnesses.
Jesus often went away to deserted places and prayed. 🙏
One day Jesus was teaching. Pharisees and teachers of the Law were sitting there; they’d come from every village in Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. The Lord’s power was with Jesus to heal.
Some men arrived carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside and lay him in front of Jesus.
They couldn’t get through the crowd, so they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles, right into the middle in front of Jesus.
Jesus saw their faith and said to the man, “My friend, your sins are forgiven.”
The legal teachers and Pharisees started debating: “Who does he think he is, speaking blasphemy? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus knew what they were thinking and answered, “Why are you arguing about this in your hearts?”
“Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or ‘Get up and walk’?”
“But so you’ll know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—“I’m telling you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
The man immediately got up in front of everyone, picked up the mat he’d been lying on, and went home praising God.
Everyone was amazed and praised God. They were filled with awe and said, “We’ve seen unbelievable things today!”
After that, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at his tax booth. He said, “Follow me!”
Levi left everything, got up, and followed him.
Levi hosted a huge feast for Jesus at his house. A big crowd of tax collectors and others were eating with them.
The Pharisees and their legal teachers complained to Jesus’ disciples: “Why are you eating and drinking with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor; sick people do.”
“I haven’t come to call people who think they’re righteous. I came to call sinners to turn back to God.”
They said to him, “John’s disciples often fast and pray, and the Pharisees’ disciples do too. But your disciples eat and drink—what’s up with that?”
Jesus said, “Can you make the groom’s friends fast while the groom is still with them?”
“The time will come when the groom is taken away from them. Then, in those days, they’ll fast.”
He also told them this parable: “Nobody cuts a patch from a new garment and sews it onto an old one. They’ll tear the new garment, and the new patch won’t match the old.”
“Nobody pours new wine into old wineskins. The new wine will burst them, spilling the wine and ruining the skins.”
“New wine has to go into fresh wineskins, and then both are preserved.”
“And nobody who’s been drinking old wine immediately wants new wine. They say, ‘The old is better.’”
On a Sabbath—the second one after the first—Jesus was walking through grain fields. His disciples picked heads of grain, rubbed them in their hands, and ate.
Some Pharisees said, “Why are you doing something the Law doesn’t allow on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and the people with him were hungry?”
“He went into God’s house, took the bread of the Presence, ate it, and shared it with his companions—even though only priests were allowed to eat it.”
Then he told them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath, Jesus went into the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was shriveled.
The legal teachers and Pharisees watched Jesus closely, waiting to see if he’d heal on the Sabbath so they could accuse him.
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He told the man with the shriveled hand, “Get up and stand here in the middle.” The man got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, “Here’s a question for you: on the Sabbath, is it right to do good or harm? To save a life or destroy one?”
He looked around at everyone and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man did, and his hand was restored, healthy like the other one.
The Pharisees were furious. They started discussing what they could do to Jesus.
Around that time, Jesus went up the mountain to pray. He spent the whole night praying to God. 🙏
When morning came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he named Peter; Andrew his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
Matthew; Thomas; James son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called the Zealot;
Judas son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

Jesus came down the mountain with them and stood on a level place. A crowd of his disciples and a huge number of people from Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal regions of Tyre and Sidon were there. They came to hear him and be healed.
People troubled by unclean spirits came too, and they were healed.
The whole crowd tried to touch Jesus, because power came from him and healed them all.
Jesus looked at his disciples and said, “You who are poor are blessed, because God’s Kingdom belongs to you.”
“You who are hungry now are blessed, because you’ll be satisfied. You who are weeping now are blessed, because you’ll laugh.”
“You’re blessed when people hate you, push you out, mock you, and call your name evil because of the Son of Man.”
“When that day comes, celebrate and leap for joy! Your reward in heaven is great. Their ancestors treated the prophets the same way. 🙌”
“But trouble is coming for you who are rich—you’ve already received your comfort.”
“Trouble for you who are full now—you’ll be hungry. Trouble for you who laugh now—you’ll mourn and weep.”
“Trouble when everyone speaks well of you. Their ancestors did the same for the false prophets.”
“But to all of you listening, I say: love your enemies. Do good to those who hate you.”
“Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.”
“If someone strikes you on one cheek, offer the other too. If someone takes your coat, don’t hold back your shirt either.”
“Give to everyone who asks you. If someone takes what belongs to you, don’t demand it back.”
“Treat people exactly as you want them to treat you.”
“If you love only the people who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love the people who love them.”
“If you do good only to people who do good to you, what credit is that? Sinners do that too.”
“If you lend only to people you expect to repay you, what credit is that? Even sinners lend to sinners to get the same amount back.”
“Instead, love your enemies, do good, and lend without expecting repayment. Your reward will be great, and you’ll be children of the Most High. God is kind even to the ungrateful and evil.”
“Be merciful, then, just as your Father is merciful.”
“Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Forgive, and you’ll be forgiven.”
“Give, and it’ll be given to you: a good measure, packed down, shaken together, and spilling over. The measure you use will be used for you too.”
Jesus told them a parable: “Can a blind person lead another blind person? Won’t they both fall into a ditch?”
“A student isn’t above their teacher. But when fully trained, each student will be like their teacher.”
“Why do you notice the tiny speck in your brother’s eye but miss the plank in your own?”

“How can you say, ‘Brother, let me get that speck out of your eye,’ when you can’t see the plank in your own? You hypocrite! First get the plank out of your eye. Then you’ll see clearly enough to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.”
“A good tree doesn’t produce rotten fruit, and a rotten tree doesn’t produce good fruit.”
“You can tell what kind of tree it is by its fruit. People don’t pick figs from thornbushes or grapes from brambles.”
“A good person brings good things out of the good stored in their heart. An evil person brings evil things out of the evil stored there. What fills the heart spills out of the mouth.”
“Why call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and then ignore what I say?”
“I’ll show you what someone is like who comes to me, hears my words, and acts on them.”
“They’re like someone building a house who dug deep and laid the foundation on rock. When floodwater surged against that house, it couldn’t shake it, because it was built on rock.”

“But whoever hears my words and doesn’t act on them is like someone who built a house on bare ground without a foundation. The flood smashed into it, and it collapsed right away. That house was completely wrecked.”
After Jesus finished speaking to the people, he went into Capernaum.
A centurion’s servant, someone he valued deeply, was sick and close to death.
When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Jesus to come and save his servant.
They came to Jesus and pleaded with him: “He deserves your help,”
“because he loves our people and built our synagogue for us.”
Jesus went with them. When he was getting close to the house, the centurion sent friends with a message: “Lord, don’t trouble yourself. I’m not worthy to have you come under my roof.”
“That’s why I didn’t think I was worthy to come to you myself. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.”
“I’m a man under authority too, with soldiers under me. I tell one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; another, ‘Come!’ and he comes. I tell my servant, ‘Do this!’ and he does it.”
Jesus was amazed when he heard this. He turned to the crowd following him and said, “I’m telling you, I haven’t found faith like this anywhere in Israel.”
When the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant well again.
Soon after, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples and a huge crowd went with him.
As he approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out—the only son of his mother, who was a widow. Many people from town were with her.
When the Lord saw her, he felt compassion for her and said, “Don’t cry.”
He came up and touched the funeral stretcher, and the people carrying it stopped. He said, “Young man, I’m telling you: get up!”
The dead man sat up and began speaking. Jesus gave him back to his mother.
Fear swept over everyone, and they praised God: “A great prophet has appeared among us!” and “God has come to help his people!”
News about Jesus spread through all Judea and the surrounding region.
John’s disciples told him about everything that was happening.
John called two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus with this question: “Are you the one who is coming, or should we expect someone else?”
The men came to Jesus and said, “John the Baptizer sent us to ask you, ‘Are you the one who is coming, or should we expect someone else?’”
Right then, Jesus healed many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits. He gave sight to many who were blind.

Jesus answered them, “Go tell John what you’ve seen and heard: blind people see, people who couldn’t walk are walking, people with leprosy are cleansed, deaf people hear, the dead are raised, and poor people hear good news.”
“The one who doesn’t stumble because of me is blessed.”
After John’s messengers left, Jesus began telling the crowd about John: “What did you go out to the wilderness to see? A reed bending in the wind?”
“What did you go out to see? Someone dressed in soft clothes? People in fancy clothes, living in luxury, are in royal palaces.”
“So what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes—and more than a prophet.”
“This is the man Scripture speaks about: ‘Look, I’m sending my messenger ahead of you to prepare your way.’”
“I’m telling you, among everyone born of women, no prophet is greater than John the Baptizer. Yet the least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he is.”
When the people and tax collectors heard this, they agreed that God was right, because they had been baptized by John.
But the Pharisees and legal experts rejected God’s purpose for them, because they hadn’t been baptized by John.
Jesus said, “What can I compare the people of this generation to? What are they like?”
“They’re like children sitting in the marketplace, calling to each other: ‘We played a flute for you, but you didn’t dance. We sang a funeral song, but you didn’t cry.’”
“John the Baptizer came without eating bread or drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’”
“The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at him—a glutton, a drunk, and a friend to tax collectors and sinners!’”
“Wisdom is shown to be right by all her children.”
One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him. Jesus went into the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
A woman in that town, known as a sinner, heard Jesus was eating at the Pharisee’s house. She brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
She stood behind Jesus at his feet, crying. Her tears fell on his feet; she wiped them with her hair, kissed his feet, and poured perfume on them.
When the Pharisee who invited Jesus saw it, he thought, “If this man were really a prophet, he’d know what kind of woman is touching him. She’s a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, go ahead.”
Jesus said, “A lender had two people who owed him money. One owed five hundred denarii, the other fifty.”
“Neither could pay him back, so he forgave both debts. Which one will love him more?”
Simon answered, “I suppose the one whose larger debt he forgave.” Jesus said, “You got it right.”

Then he turned toward the woman and said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house, and you didn’t give me water for my feet. She washed my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.”
“You didn’t greet me with a kiss, but since I came in, she hasn’t stopped kissing my feet.”
“You didn’t put oil on my head, but she poured perfume on my feet.”
“So I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven; that’s why she has shown such great love. But whoever is forgiven little loves little.”
Jesus told the woman, “Your sins are forgiven.”
The people at the table began asking themselves, “Who is this, that he even forgives sins?”
But Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
After that, Jesus traveled through towns and villages, preaching and sharing the good news of God’s Kingdom. The twelve were with him,
along with some women who had been healed of evil spirits and sickness: Mary, called Magdalene, who had been freed from seven demons;
Joanna, wife of Chuza, Herod’s manager; Susanna; and many others. They used their own resources to support Jesus and the disciples.
A huge crowd gathered, with people coming from town after town. Jesus taught them through a parable:
“A farmer went out to scatter seed. As he scattered it, some fell beside the road, got trampled, and birds ate it up.”
“Some fell on rock. It sprouted, then dried up because it had no moisture.”
“Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew alongside it and choked it.”
“Some fell in good soil. It grew and produced a hundred times what was planted.” Then Jesus called out, “If you have ears to hear, listen!” 🌱
His disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
He said, “You’ve been given the chance to know the secrets of God’s Kingdom. The others get parables, so that ‘they may look but not see, and hear but not understand.’”
“Here’s what the parable means: the seed is God’s word.”
“The seed beside the road is people who hear. Then the devil comes and snatches the word from their hearts, so they won’t believe and be saved.”
“The seed on rock is people who hear the word and welcome it with joy. But they have no roots. They believe for a while, then fall away when testing comes.”
“The seed among thorns is people who hear, but as they go through life, worries, wealth, and pleasures choke them. Their fruit never matures.”
“The seed in good soil is people with honest and good hearts. They hear the word, hold on to it, and keep producing fruit with perseverance.”
“Nobody lights a lamp and covers it with a bowl or hides it under a bed. They put it on a stand so everyone who comes in can see the light.”
“Nothing hidden will stay hidden forever. Secrets will be uncovered and brought out into the open.”
“So pay attention to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more; whoever doesn’t have will lose even what they think they have.”
Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see him, but the crowd was so packed they couldn’t get near him.
Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are outside, trying to see you.”
He answered, “My mother and brothers are the people who hear God’s word and do it.”
One day Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and told them, “Let’s cross to the other side of the lake.” So they set out.
As they sailed, Jesus fell asleep. A windstorm swept down on the lake, and the boat started filling with dangerous amounts of water.
They came and woke him: “Master, Master, we’re going to die!” He got up, rebuked the wind and raging water, and they stopped. Everything went calm.
He asked them, “Where’s your faith?” They were afraid and amazed, saying to each other, “Who is this? He commands even the wind and water, and they obey him!”
They arrived in the region of the Gadarenes, across the lake from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped onto land, a man from the town met him. Demons had controlled him for a long time. He wore no clothes and lived in tombs, not in a house.
When he saw Jesus, he shouted and fell in front of him: “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Please, don’t torment me!”

Jesus had been ordering the unclean spirit to come out. It often seized the man, who was kept under guard and chained hand and foot. He broke the restraints, and the demon drove him out into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, “What’s your name?” He said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
The demons begged Jesus not to order them into the abyss.
A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside. The demons begged him to let them enter the pigs, and he allowed it.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
The people tending the pigs saw what happened, ran off, and reported it in town and out in the countryside.
People went out to see for themselves. They came to Jesus and found the man the demons had left, sitting at Jesus’ feet, dressed and in his right mind. They were afraid.
The people who had seen it told everyone how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
All the people from the surrounding region of the Gadarenes asked Jesus to leave because they were terrified. So he got into the boat and went back.
The man the demons had left begged Jesus to let him come along. But Jesus sent him home, saying:
“Go back to your house and tell people everything God has done for you.” The man went through the whole town, telling everyone what Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him. They’d all been waiting for him.
A man named Jairus came up. He was a synagogue leader. He fell at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come to his house,
because his only daughter, about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed in around him.
A woman had been bleeding for twelve years. She’d spent everything she had on doctors, but nobody could heal her.
She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of his cloak. Right away, the bleeding stopped.
Jesus asked, “Who touched me?” Everyone denied it. Peter and those with him said, “Master, all these people are pressing in and bumping you, and you ask, ‘Who touched me?’”
But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me. I felt power go out from me.”
When the woman realized she couldn’t stay hidden, she came trembling and fell in front of him. In front of everyone, she explained why she touched him and how she’d been healed instantly.
Jesus told her, “Daughter, take heart. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader’s house: “Your daughter has died. Don’t trouble the Teacher anymore.”
Jesus heard and told Jairus, “Don’t be afraid. Just believe, and she’ll be healed.”
When Jesus reached the house, he didn’t let anyone go in with him except Peter, John, James, the girl’s father, and her mother.
Everyone was crying and mourning for her, but Jesus said, “Don’t cry. She isn’t dead; she’s sleeping.”
They laughed at him, because they knew she was dead.
Jesus sent them all outside. Then he took the girl by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”
Her spirit returned, and she immediately got up. Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were completely amazed, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
Jesus called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them out to announce God’s Kingdom and heal the sick.
He told them, “Take nothing for the road: no walking stick, bag, bread, or money. Don’t bring a spare shirt.”
“When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that town.”
“If people won’t welcome you, leave that town and shake even its dust from your feet as a witness against them.”
The disciples set out and traveled through the villages, sharing the good news and healing people everywhere.
Herod the ruler heard about everything happening through Jesus and was confused. Some people were saying John had risen from the dead,
others said Elijah had appeared, and still others said one of the prophets from long ago had come back.
Herod said, “I had John beheaded, so who is this I keep hearing about?” He kept trying to see Jesus.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus everything they had done. He took them along and slipped away to a deserted area near Bethsaida.
But the crowds found out and followed him. Jesus welcomed them, taught them about God’s Kingdom, and healed those who needed it.
The day was getting late. The twelve came to him and said, “Send the crowd away to nearby villages and farms to find food and a place to stay. We’re out in the middle of nowhere.”
But Jesus said, “You give them something to eat.” They replied, “We have only five loaves and two fish—unless we go buy food for all these people.”
There were about five thousand men. Jesus told his disciples, “Have them sit in groups of about fifty.”
They did that and got everyone seated.
Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to serve the crowd.
Everyone ate and was satisfied. The disciples gathered twelve baskets of leftover pieces. 🍞
One day, while Jesus was praying alone and the disciples were nearby, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say I am?”
They answered, “John the Baptizer. Others say Elijah, and some say a prophet from long ago has come back.”
He asked them, “And who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “God’s Christ.”
Jesus warned them and ordered them not to tell anyone.
He said, “The Son of Man must suffer many things. The elders, chief priests, and legal teachers will reject him. He’ll be killed, and on the third day he’ll be raised.”
Then he said to everyone, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must say no to themselves, pick up their cross, and follow me.”
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for my sake will save it.”
“What good is it to gain the whole world if you lose yourself or ruin your life?”
“Whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory, the Father’s glory, and the glory of the holy angels.”
“I’m telling you the truth: some people standing here won’t die before they see God’s Kingdom.”
About eight days later, Jesus took Peter, John, and James with him up the mountain to pray.
As he prayed, his face changed, and his clothes became dazzling white.
Suddenly, two men—Moses and Elijah—were talking with him.
They appeared in glory and spoke about Jesus’ departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep. But when they woke up fully, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with him.
As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it’s good we’re here. Let’s build three shelters—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He didn’t know what he was saying.
While he was still speaking, a cloud came and covered them. They were afraid as the cloud surrounded them.
A voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was there alone. The disciples kept quiet and didn’t tell anyone then what they had seen.
The next day, when Jesus and the disciples came down from the mountain, a huge crowd met him.
A man in the crowd shouted, “Teacher, please look at my son! He’s my only child.”
“A spirit grabs him, and he suddenly screams. It throws him into convulsions until he foams at the mouth. It keeps hurting him badly and hardly ever leaves him.”
“I begged your disciples to drive it out, but they couldn’t.”
Jesus answered, “You unbelieving and twisted generation! How long must I stay with you and put up with this? Bring your son here.”
As the boy was coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and returned him to his father.
Everyone was amazed by God’s greatness. While they were still marveling at everything Jesus did, he told his disciples:
“Listen carefully: the Son of Man is about to be handed over to people.”
But they didn’t understand what he meant. It was hidden from them, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
Then an argument started among them about which one was the greatest.
Jesus knew what they were reasoning in their hearts. He took a little child and stood the child beside him.
He told them, “Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. The least among you all—that person is great.”
John said, “Master, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him because he doesn’t follow with us.”
Jesus told him, “Don’t stop him. Whoever isn’t against us is for us.”
As the time drew near for Jesus to be taken up, he firmly set his face toward Jerusalem
and sent messengers ahead. They entered a Samaritan village to get things ready for him.
But the people there wouldn’t welcome him, because he was headed for Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said, “Lord, should we call fire down from heaven to destroy them, like Elijah did?”
Jesus turned and rebuked them: “You don’t know what kind of spirit you’re acting from.”
“The Son of Man didn’t come to destroy people’s lives, but to save them.” Then they went to another village.
As they continued on the road, someone said to Jesus, “Lord, I’ll follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus told him, “Foxes have dens, and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
He told another person, “Follow me.” But the man said, “Lord, first let me go bury my father.”
Jesus said, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
Someone else said, “I’ll follow you, Lord, but first let me say goodbye to my family at home.”
Jesus told him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and keeps looking back is fit for God’s Kingdom.”
After this, the Lord appointed seventy other disciples and sent them ahead in pairs to every town and place he planned to visit.
He told them, “The harvest is huge, but the workers are few. So ask the Lord of the harvest to send more workers into his fields.”
“Go on your way. Look, I’m sending you out like lambs among wolves.”
“Don’t bring a purse, bag, or sandals, and don’t stop to greet people along the road.”
“When you enter a house, first say, ‘Peace to this home.’”
“If someone there is open to peace, your peace will rest on them. If not, it will come back to you.”
“Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they give you. Workers deserve their pay. Don’t keep moving from house to house.”
“When you enter a town and people welcome you, eat what they set in front of you.”
“Heal the sick there and tell them, ‘God’s Kingdom has come close to you.’”
“But when you enter a town and people don’t welcome you, go out into its streets and say:”
“‘Even the dust from your town stuck to our feet—we’re wiping it off as a warning to you. Still, know this: God’s Kingdom has come close.’”
“I’m telling you, on judgment day Sodom will have an easier time than that town.”

“How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the mighty works done in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would’ve turned back to God long ago, wearing sackcloth and sitting in ashes.”
“But Tyre and Sidon will have an easier judgment than you.”
“And you, Capernaum—do you think you’ll be lifted up to heaven? You’ll be brought down to Hades.”
“Whoever listens to you listens to me. Whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”
The seventy came back full of joy: “Lord, even the demons obey us when we use your name!”
Jesus said, “I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.”
“Look, I’ve given you authority to walk over snakes and scorpions and over all the enemy’s power. Nothing will harm you.”
“But don’t celebrate because the spirits obey you. Celebrate because your names are written in heaven.”

In that moment, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I thank you: you’ve hidden these things from the wise and clever and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, because that’s what pleased you.”
“My Father has handed everything over to me. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to reveal him to.”
Jesus turned privately to his disciples and said, “You’re blessed to see what you’re seeing.”
“I’m telling you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see but didn’t see it, and to hear what you hear but didn’t hear it.”
A legal expert stood up to test Jesus: “Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus asked him, “What’s written in the Law? How do you understand it?”
He answered, “Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind—and love your neighbor as yourself.”
Jesus said, “You answered correctly. Live that way, and you’ll have life.”
But the man wanted to justify himself, so he asked Jesus, “And who counts as my neighbor?”
Jesus answered, “A man was traveling down from Jerusalem to Jericho when robbers jumped him. They stripped him, beat him, and left him half dead.”
“By chance, a priest was traveling that road. He saw the man and crossed to the other side.”
“A Levite came to the same spot, saw him, and crossed over too.”
“But a Samaritan traveling that way came across him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.”
“He went over, bandaged his wounds, and poured on oil and wine. Then he put the man on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.”
“The next day, he gave the innkeeper two denarii and said, ‘Take care of him. If you spend more, I’ll pay you back when I return.’”
“Which of these three acted like a neighbor to the man attacked by robbers?”
The legal expert said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus told him, “Go and do the same.”
As they continued traveling, Jesus entered a village, where a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
Her sister Mary sat at Jesus’ feet, listening to what he said.
Martha was distracted by all the hosting. She came over and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to do everything alone? Tell her to help me!”
Jesus answered, “Martha, Martha, you’re anxious and stressed about so many things.”
“But one thing is needed. Mary chose what’s good, and nobody will take it away from her.”
After Jesus finished praying in one place, a disciple asked him, “Lord, teach us to pray, like John taught his disciples.”
Jesus said, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will happen on earth just as in heaven.”
“‘Give us the bread we need each day.”
“‘Forgive our sins, because we forgive everyone who owes us. Don’t bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.’”
Then he said, “Suppose you go to a friend’s house at midnight and say, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread.”
“‘A friend of mine just arrived after a long trip, and I have nothing to serve him.’”
“Suppose your friend calls from inside, ‘Don’t bother me. The door’s locked, and my children are in bed with me. I can’t get up and give you anything.’”
“I’m telling you, even if he won’t get up just because you’re friends, he’ll get up because you keep asking and give you whatever you need.”
“So keep asking, and you’ll receive. Keep searching, and you’ll find. Keep knocking, and the door will open for you.”
“Everyone who asks receives; everyone who searches finds; and the door opens for everyone who knocks.”
“Which father among you would hand his son a stone when he asks for bread? Or give him a snake when he asks for a fish?”
“Or if he asks for an egg, would you give him a scorpion?”
“Even you, with all your sin, know how to give good gifts to your children. How much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!”
Jesus was driving out a demon that kept a man from speaking. When the demon left, the man spoke, and the crowd was amazed.
But some people said, “He drives out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
Others tested Jesus by demanding a sign from heaven.
Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Every kingdom divided against itself falls apart, and a divided household collapses.”
“If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? You say I drive out demons by Beelzebul.”
“If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, then who do your people drive them out by? They’ll be your judges.”
“But if I drive out demons by God’s finger, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.”
“When a strong, armed man guards his own home, his possessions are safe.”
“But when someone stronger attacks and beats him, they take away the armor he trusted and divide up the goods.”
“Whoever isn’t with me is against me. Whoever doesn’t gather with me scatters.”
“When an unclean spirit leaves someone, it wanders through dry places looking for rest. When it can’t find any, it says, ‘I’ll go back to the home I left.’”
“When it returns, it finds the place swept clean and put in order.”
“Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself. They move in and settle there, and that person ends up worse than before.”
While Jesus was saying this, a woman in the crowd called out, “Blessed is the mother who gave birth to you and nursed you!”
But he said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear God’s word and keep it.”
As the crowds kept gathering, Jesus began saying, “This generation is evil. It keeps demanding a sign, but no sign will be given except the sign of Jonah the prophet.”
“Just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.”

“The Queen of the South will stand up at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them. She came from far away to hear Solomon’s wisdom—and look, someone greater than Solomon is here.”
“The people of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it. They turned back to God when Jonah preached—and look, someone greater than Jonah is here.”
“Nobody lights a lamp and hides it in a cellar or under a basket. They put it on a stand so people coming in can see the light.”
“Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light. When it’s unhealthy, your body is full of darkness.”
“So check yourself: make sure the light you think you have isn’t actually darkness.”
“If your whole body is full of light, with no darkness in it, you’ll be completely lit up, like when a lamp shines its light on you.”
While Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited him to eat. Jesus went in and reclined at the table.
The Pharisee was surprised that Jesus didn’t first wash before the meal.
The Lord said to him, “You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and plate, but inside you’re full of greed and evil.”
“You fools! Didn’t the one who made the outside make the inside too?”
“Give to the needy out of what is within, and everything will be clean for you.”
“How terrible for you Pharisees! You carefully tithe mint, rue, and every herb, but you skip justice and love for God. You should’ve done those things without neglecting the others.”
“How terrible for you! You love the best seats in the synagogues and the respectful greetings in the marketplaces.”
“How terrible for you legal teachers and Pharisees—you hypocrites! You’re like hidden graves that people walk over without knowing.”
One of the legal experts said, “Teacher, when you say that, you’re insulting us too.”
Jesus said, “How terrible for you legal experts too! You pile heavy burdens on people, but you won’t lift even one finger to help them.”
“How terrible for you! You build tombs for the prophets, but your ancestors killed them.”
“So you’re witnesses who approve what your ancestors did: they killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.”
“That’s why God’s wisdom said, ‘I’ll send them prophets and apostles. They’ll kill and persecute some of them,”
“‘so this generation will be held responsible for the blood of all the prophets shed since the world began—”
“‘from Abel’s blood to Zechariah’s blood, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I’m telling you, this generation will be held responsible.”
“How terrible for you legal experts! You took away the key to knowledge. You didn’t go in yourselves, and you blocked the people who were trying to enter.”
When Jesus left, the legal teachers and Pharisees became furious and began pressing him with all kinds of questions,
lying in wait and trying to catch him saying something they could use to accuse him.
Thousands of people had gathered, packed so tightly that they were stepping on each other. Jesus began by telling his disciples, “Watch out for the Pharisees’ yeast—that’s their hypocrisy.”
“Nothing covered up will stay hidden; nothing kept secret won’t be uncovered.”
“Whatever you say in the dark will be heard in daylight. What you whisper in a back room will be announced from the rooftops.”
“I’m telling you, my friends: don’t fear people who can kill the body and then can’t do anything else to you.”
“I’ll tell you who to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw you into Gehenna. Yes, fear him.”
“Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Yet God doesn’t forget a single one.”
“Even the hairs on your head are all counted. So don’t be afraid—you matter more than a whole flock of sparrows.”
“I’m telling you: everyone who acknowledges me in front of people, the Son of Man will acknowledge in front of God’s angels.”
“But whoever disowns me in front of people will be disowned in front of God’s angels.”
“Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven.”
“When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, don’t panic about how to defend yourself or what to say.”
“The Holy Spirit will teach you in that very moment what you need to say.”
Someone in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, tell my brother to split the inheritance with me.”
Jesus answered, “Man, who made me your judge or the one who divides your inheritance?”
He told them, “Watch out. Guard yourselves against greed. A person’s life isn’t measured by how much stuff they own.”
Then Jesus told them a parable: “A rich man’s land produced an abundant harvest.”
“He thought to himself, ‘What am I going to do? I don’t have room to store all my crops.’”
“Then he said, ‘Here’s the plan: I’ll tear down my barns, build bigger ones, and store all my grain and goods there.”
“‘Then I’ll tell myself, “You’ve got plenty saved up for years. Take it easy—eat, drink, and enjoy life.”’”
“But God said to him, ‘You fool! Tonight your life will be demanded from you. Who’s going to get all the things you stored up?’”
“That’s how it goes for anyone who stores up wealth for themselves but isn’t rich toward God.”
Jesus told his disciples, “So I’m telling you: don’t worry about your life—what you’ll eat—or your body—what you’ll wear.”
“Life is more than food, and your body is more than clothes.”
“Think about the ravens: they don’t plant or harvest, they have no storeroom or barn, yet God feeds them. You’re worth so much more than birds!”
“Can any of you add even a tiny amount to your height by worrying?”
“If you can’t do even that little thing, why stress about everything else?”
“Look at how lilies grow. They don’t work or make clothes, but I’m telling you, even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one of them.”
“If God dresses the grass in the field—which is here today and tossed into the oven tomorrow—won’t he dress you too, you of little faith?”
“So don’t keep chasing what you’ll eat or drink, and don’t stay worried.”
“The nations of the world chase all those things, but your Father knows you need them.”
“Instead, seek God’s Kingdom, and these things will be given to you too.”
“Don’t be afraid, little flock. Your Father is happy to give you the Kingdom.”
“Sell what you own and give to people in need. Make purses for yourselves that won’t wear out—lasting treasure in heaven, where no thief gets near and no moth destroys.”
“Where your treasure is, that’s where your heart will be too.”
“Be dressed and ready for action, with your lamps burning.”
“Be like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding feast, ready to open the door as soon as he knocks.”
“Blessed are the servants the master finds awake when he returns. I’m telling you the truth: he’ll dress for work, seat them at the table, and serve them himself.”
“They’re blessed if he comes in the middle of the night or even near dawn and finds them ready.”
“Remember: if a homeowner knew when the thief was coming, they’d stay awake and wouldn’t let their house get broken into.”
“So stay ready too. The Son of Man is coming at an hour you don’t expect.”
Peter asked, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
The Lord said, “Who is the faithful and wise manager? The one his master puts in charge of the household to give everyone their food at the right time.”
“Blessed is that servant if the master returns and finds them doing their job.”
“I’m telling you the truth: the master will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.”
“But suppose that servant thinks, ‘My master’s taking forever,’ and starts beating the men and women servants, eating, drinking, and getting drunk.”
“The master will come on a day the servant doesn’t expect and at an hour they don’t know. He’ll cut the servant in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.”
“The servant who knew the master’s will but didn’t get ready or do what he wanted will receive many blows.”
“But the one who didn’t know and did things deserving punishment will receive fewer blows. Much will be required from everyone given much, and even more will be asked of the one trusted with much.”
“I came to cast fire on the earth, and I wish it were already burning.”
“But I have a baptism to go through, and I’m under great pressure until it’s completed!”
“Do you think I came to bring peace on earth? I’m telling you, no—I came to bring division.”
“From now on, five people in one household will be split: three against two, and two against three.”
“They’ll be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
Jesus also said to the crowd, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say right away, ‘Rain’s coming,’ and it does.”
“When the south wind blows, you say, ‘It’s going to be scorching,’ and it is.”
“Hypocrites! You know how to read the sky and the land. How come you can’t read what’s happening right now?”
“Why don’t you judge for yourselves what’s right?”

“When you’re going with your opponent to court, do your best to settle things on the way. Otherwise they may drag you before the judge, the judge hand you to the officer, and the officer throw you in prison.”
“I’m telling you, you won’t get out until you’ve paid the very last coin.”
Some people there told Jesus about the Galileans Pilate had killed while they were offering sacrifices, mixing their blood with the sacrifices.
Jesus answered, “Do you think those Galileans were worse sinners than everybody else in Galilee because they suffered like that?”
I’m telling you, no. But unless you turn back to God, you’ll all perish too.
“What about the eighteen people the tower in Siloam fell on and killed? Do you think they were worse offenders than everyone else in Jerusalem?”
“I’m telling you, no. But unless you turn back to God, you’ll all perish too.”
Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit, but found none.”
“He said to the gardener, ‘Look, for three years I’ve come looking for fruit on this fig tree and found none. Cut it down! Why should it keep wasting the soil?’”
“The gardener answered, ‘Sir, leave it alone for one more year. I’ll dig around it and put manure on it.”
“‘If it bears fruit next year, great. If not, then cut it down.’”
Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
A woman was there who had been bent over for eighteen years because of a spirit that made her ill. She couldn’t stand up straight at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said, “Woman, you’re freed from your illness.”
He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and praised God. 🙌
But the synagogue leader was angry that Jesus healed on the Sabbath. He told the crowd, “There are six days for work. Come get healed on those days, not on the Sabbath!”
The Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Don’t each of you untie your ox or donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead it out for water?”
“Shouldn’t this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan kept bound for eighteen long years, be freed from that bondage on the Sabbath?”
When Jesus said this, his opponents were ashamed, and the crowd celebrated all the wonderful things he was doing.
Then Jesus said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? What can I compare it to?”
“It’s like a mustard seed someone planted in a garden. It grew into a large tree, and birds nested in its branches.” 🌳
Again he said, “What can I compare God’s Kingdom to?”
“It’s like yeast a woman mixed into three measures of flour until the whole batch rose.”
Jesus continued through towns and villages, teaching as he traveled toward Jerusalem.
Someone asked him, “Lord, will only a few people be saved?” He answered them:
“Work hard to enter through the narrow door. I’m telling you, many will try to enter but won’t be able.”
“Once the homeowner gets up and shuts the door, you’ll be standing outside, knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open up!’ He’ll answer, ‘I don’t know you or where you’re from.’”
“Then you’ll say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’”
“But he’ll say, ‘I don’t know where you’re from. Get away from me, all you who do evil.’”
“There’ll be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, while you’re thrown outside.”
“People will come from the east, west, north, and south and take their places in God’s Kingdom.”
“Look, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”
That same day, some Pharisees came and told Jesus, “Get out of here and go somewhere else. Herod wants to kill you.”
He said to them, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I’m driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I’ll finish my work.’”
“But I must keep going today, tomorrow, and the day after, because a prophet can’t be killed anywhere but Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and stone the messengers sent to you. How many times I wanted to gather your children together like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings—but you refused!”
“Look, your house is left desolate. I’m telling you, you won’t see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name!’”
One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat at the home of a prominent Pharisee. Everyone there was watching him closely.
A man suffering from swelling was in front of him.
Jesus asked the legal experts and Pharisees, “Is it allowed to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
But they stayed silent. Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
Then he said to them, “If your child or ox falls into a well on the Sabbath, which of you wouldn’t pull them out right away?”
They couldn’t answer him.
Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, so he told them this story:
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, don’t take the place of honor. Someone more distinguished than you may have been invited,
and then the host who invited both of you will come and say, ‘Give this person your place.’ Then you’ll have to move down in disgrace.
Instead, when you’re invited, take the lowest place. Then the host may come and say, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ That will bring you honor in front of everyone at the table.
For those who lift themselves up will be brought down, and those who humble themselves will be lifted up.”
Then Jesus said to his host, “When you give a lunch or dinner, don’t invite your friends, brothers, relatives, or rich neighbors. They may invite you back, and you’ll be repaid.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind.
Then you’ll be blessed, because they can’t repay you. You’ll be repaid when the righteous are raised.”
When one of the people eating with Jesus heard this, he said, “Blessed is the one who will feast in God’s kingdom!”
Jesus replied, “A man prepared a great dinner and invited many guests.
At dinner time, he sent his servant to tell them, ‘Come, everything is ready now.’
But they all began making excuses. The first said, ‘I bought a field and need to go see it. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I bought five pairs of oxen and need to try them out. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I just got married, so I can’t come.’
The servant came back and reported this. The angry homeowner told him, ‘Go quickly into the streets and alleys of the town and bring in the poor, disabled, blind, and lame.’
The servant said, ‘Sir, I’ve done what you ordered, but there’s still room.’
The master said, ‘Go out to the roads and country lanes and urge people to come in, so my house will be full.
I tell you, none of those who were invited will taste my dinner.’”
Large crowds were traveling with Jesus. He turned to them and said,
“If anyone comes to me and doesn’t hate their father, mother, wife, children, brothers and sisters—even their own life—they can’t be my disciple.
Whoever doesn’t carry their own cross and follow me can’t be my disciple.
Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Won’t you first sit down and figure out the cost to see if you can finish it?
Otherwise, if you lay the foundation but can’t finish, everyone who sees it will make fun of you,
saying, ‘This person started building but couldn’t finish.’
Or what king going to war against another king won’t first sit down and consider whether he can meet the enemy’s twenty thousand soldiers with his own ten thousand?
If he can’t, he’ll send a delegation while the other king is still far away and ask for peace terms.
In the same way, none of you can be my disciple unless you give up everything you have.
“Salt is good, but if it loses its flavor, how can it be made salty again?
It’s not useful for the soil or the manure pile; it gets thrown away. Anyone with ears to hear should listen.”
All the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around Jesus to hear him.
The Pharisees and legal experts grumbled, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
So Jesus told them this story:
“Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one. Wouldn’t you leave the ninety-nine in the open country and search for the lost one until you find it?
When you find it, you joyfully put it on your shoulders
and go home. Then you call your friends and neighbors together and say, ‘Celebrate with me—I found my lost sheep!’
I tell you, in the same way there’ll be more joy in heaven over one sinner who turns back to God than over ninety-nine righteous people who don’t think they need to repent.
“Or suppose a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. Won’t she light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?
When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors and says, ‘Celebrate with me—I found my lost coin!’
In the same way, I tell you, there is joy among God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”
Jesus continued, “A man had two sons.
The younger one said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of the property.’ So the father divided his estate between them.
A few days later, the younger son gathered everything he had and traveled to a distant country, where he wasted his money on wild living.
After he’d spent everything, a severe famine hit that country, and he began to go without.
He went and hired himself out to one of the citizens there, who sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
He was so hungry he wanted to eat the pods the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
“Then he came to his senses and said, ‘All my father’s hired workers have more than enough food, and here I am starving!
I’ll get up, go to my father, and say, “Father, I’ve sinned against heaven and against you.
I’m no longer worthy to be called your son. Treat me like one of your hired workers.”’
So he got up and went to his father. While he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion. He ran to his son, hugged him, and kissed him.
The son said, ‘Father, I’ve sinned against heaven and against you. I’m no longer worthy to be called your son.’
“But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let’s eat and celebrate,
because this son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ And they began to celebrate.
“Meanwhile, the older son was out in the field. As he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
The servant told him, ‘Your brother has come home, and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has him back safe and sound.’
The older brother became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I’ve worked like a slave for you and never disobeyed you. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours comes back, after wasting your property on prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
The father said, ‘My son, you’re always with me, and everything I have is yours.
But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
Jesus also told his disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his property.
He called the manager in and said, ‘What’s this I hear about you? Turn in your accounts, because you can’t be my manager anymore.’
“The manager thought to himself, ‘What will I do now? My master is taking away my job. I’m not strong enough to dig, and I’m too ashamed to beg.
I know what I’ll do, so people will welcome me into their homes after I lose my job.’
He called in each of his master’s debtors. He asked the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
The man answered, ‘A hundred measures of olive oil.’ The manager said, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and change it to fifty.’
Then he asked another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He answered, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ The manager said, ‘Take your bill and change it to eighty.’
“The master praised the dishonest manager because he’d acted shrewdly. People of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than people who belong to the light.
I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it’s gone, you’ll be welcomed into eternal homes.
Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
So if you haven’t been trustworthy with worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?
And if you haven’t been trustworthy with someone else’s property, who will give you property of your own?
“No servant can serve two masters. They’ll hate one and love the other, or be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and money.”
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and sneered at Jesus.
He said to them, “You’re the ones who make yourselves look righteous in front of people, but God knows your hearts. What people value highly is disgusting to God.
“The law and the prophets were proclaimed until John. Since then, the good news of God’s kingdom has been preached, and everyone is pressing their way into it.
But it’s easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for even the smallest stroke of a letter in the law to fail.
“Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. And anyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
“There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.
A poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores, was laid at the rich man’s gate.
He longed to eat the scraps falling from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
The poor man died, and angels carried him to Abraham’s side. The rich man also died and was buried.
