In Hades, where he was suffering, the rich man looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus beside him.
He called out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I’m in agony in this fire.’
“But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that during your life you received good things, while Lazarus received bad things. Now he’s comforted here, and you’re suffering.
Besides, a wide chasm has been fixed between us and you. Those who want to cross from here to you can’t, and no one can cross from there to us.’
“The rich man said, ‘Then please, father, send Lazarus to my father’s house—
I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so they won’t end up in this place of torment too.’
“But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. They should listen to them.’
“‘No, father Abraham,’ the man said. ‘But if someone goes to them from the dead, they’ll turn back to God.’
“Abraham said, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, they won’t be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.’”
Jesus told his disciples, “Things that trip people up are bound to happen. But woe to the person who causes it!” ⚠️
“It’d be better for that person to have a millstone tied around their neck and be thrown into the sea than to make one of these little ones stumble.”
“Watch yourselves. If your brother or sister sins against you, call them on it. If they turn back, forgive them.”
“Even if they sin against you seven times in one day and come back seven times saying, ‘I repent,’ forgive them.” 🤝
The apostles said to the Lord, “Grow our faith!” 🙏
The Lord replied, “If your faith were as small as a mustard seed, you could tell this sycamore tree, ‘Pull up your roots and plant yourself in the sea!’ and it would obey.”
“Suppose one of you has a servant plowing or tending sheep. When the servant gets back from the field, would you say, ‘Come sit down and eat right away’?”
“Wouldn’t you say instead, ‘Get my supper ready, dress for work, and serve me while I eat and drink. Then you can eat and drink’?”
“Does the master thank the servant just for doing what was ordered? No, that’s the servant’s duty.”
“So you too, when you’ve done everything you were told, say, ‘We’re unworthy servants; we’ve only done our duty.’”
As Jesus continued toward Jerusalem, he traveled along the border between Samaria and Galilee. 🛤️
When he entered a village, ten men with leprosy came to meet him. They stood at a distance,
calling out, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
When Jesus saw them, he said, “Go show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed. ✨
One of them saw he was healed, turned back, and loudly praised God.
He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus said, “Weren’t all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?”
“Was nobody found to come back and give glory to God except this foreigner?”
Then Jesus told him, “Get up and go on your way. Your faith has made you well.”
The Pharisees asked Jesus when God’s Kingdom would come. He answered, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t arrive with signs you can spot by watching for them.”
“Nobody will say, ‘Look, it’s here!’ or ‘There it is!’ because God’s Kingdom is already within you.”
Jesus told his disciples, “The time will come when you’ll long to see even one day of the Son of Man, but you won’t see it.”
“People will tell you, ‘Look, he’s here!’ or ‘Look, he’s over there!’ Don’t run after them.”
“Just like lightning flashes from one side of the sky to the other, the Son of Man will be on his day. ⚡”
“But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.”
“When the Son of Man comes, it’ll be like it was in Noah’s time.”
“People ate, drank, married, and were given in marriage right up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and wiped them all out.”
“It was the same in Lot’s time: people ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and built.”
“But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all. 🔥”
“That’s how it’ll be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.”
“On that day, if someone is on the roof while their belongings are inside, don’t go back down to get them. If someone is out in the field, don’t turn back.”
“Remember Lot’s wife!”
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life will preserve it.”
“I’m telling you: that night, two people will be in one bed. One will be taken, and the other left.”
“Two people will be grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other left.”
They asked him, “Where, Lord?” He answered, “Where the body is, that’s where the vultures gather.” 🦅
Jesus told them a story to make the point: keep praying, keep showing up, and don’t give up. 🙏
He said, “In one town, there was a judge who didn’t respect God or care what people thought.”
“A widow in that town kept coming back: ‘Give me justice against the person who’s coming for me!’”
“For a while, the judge said no. But then he thought, ‘I don’t respect God or care what people think;’”
“‘still, this widow keeps wearing me down. I’ll give her justice so she doesn’t keep coming back and exhausting me.’”
The Lord said, “Hear what that crooked judge is saying.”
“Won’t God bring justice for his chosen people, the ones calling out to him day and night? Is he really gonna keep putting them off?”
“I’m telling you, he’ll bring them justice soon. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith still standing on earth?”
Jesus told another story to some people who were sure they were righteous and looked down on everybody else:
“Two men went to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee; the other was a tax collector.”
“The Pharisee stood and prayed like this: ‘God, I thank you I’m not like everybody else—robbers, cheaters, adulterers, or even that tax collector over there.’”
“‘I fast twice a week and give a tenth of everything I get.’”
“But the tax collector stood way back. He wouldn’t even look up to heaven; he beat his chest and said, ‘God, please have mercy on me—I’m a sinner.’”
“I’m telling you, that man went home right with God, not the other one. Whoever bigs themselves up will be brought low; whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up.”
People were bringing even their babies to Jesus so he could touch them. The disciples saw it and started telling the people off.
Jesus called the children over: “Let the little ones come to me. Don’t block them—God’s Kingdom belongs to people like them.”
“I’m telling you the truth: if you don’t welcome God’s Kingdom like a little child, you won’t enter it.”
A ruler asked Jesus, “Good Teacher, what do I need to do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said, “Why call me good? No one is good except God alone.”
“You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery. Don’t murder. Don’t steal. Don’t give false testimony. Honor your father and mother.’”
He said, “I’ve kept all those since I was young.”
When Jesus heard him, he said, “You’re still missing one thing. Sell everything you own and give the money to the poor. Then you’ll have treasure in heaven. After that, come follow me.”
When the ruler heard that, he got seriously sad—he was extremely wealthy.
Jesus saw how sad he was and said, “How hard it is for rich people to enter God’s Kingdom!”
“A camel getting through a needle’s eye is easier than a rich person getting into God’s Kingdom.”
The people listening asked, “Then who can be saved?”
He said, “What people can’t do, God can.”
Peter said, “Look, we left everything and followed you.”
Jesus said, “I’m telling you the truth: nobody who left home, wife, brothers, parents, or children for God’s Kingdom”—
“—will miss out on receiving many times more in this life, and eternal life in the age to come.”
Jesus took the twelve aside: “Listen, we’re heading to Jerusalem. Everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man is about to happen.”
“He’ll be handed over to the Gentiles. They’ll clown him, shame him, and spit on him.”
“They’ll whip him and kill him. On the third day, he’ll rise again.”
The disciples didn’t get what he meant. It was hidden from them, and they couldn’t put the pieces together.
As Jesus got close to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
He heard the crowd moving past and asked what was going on.
They told him, “Jesus from Nazareth is passing by!”
He shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
The people up front told him to be quiet, but he shouted even louder: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and told them to bring the man over. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, I want to see again.”
Jesus told him, “See again. Your faith has made you well.”
Right away he could see. He followed Jesus and praised God, and when everybody saw it, they praised God too. 🙌
Jesus entered Jericho and was walking through town.
There was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector—and he was loaded.
He was trying to catch a look at Jesus, but the crowd was in the way. Zacchaeus was short, so he couldn’t see over them.
He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree, because Jesus was about to pass that way.
When Jesus reached the spot, he looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down! I need to stay at your place today.”
Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed him with joy.
Everybody saw it and started grumbling: “He’s gone to stay with a sinner?”
Zacchaeus stood up and told the Lord, “Look, Lord, I’m giving half my stuff to the poor. And if I’ve cheated anybody, I’ll pay them back four times over.”
Jesus said, “Today, salvation has come to this house. This man is Abraham’s son too.”
“The Son of Man came to look for and save the people who were lost.”
While they were listening, Jesus told another story because he was near Jerusalem, and they thought God’s Kingdom was about to show up right away.
He said, “A nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and then come back.”
“He called ten of his servants, gave them ten minas, and said, ‘Do business with this until I get back.’”
“But his people hated him. They sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man ruling over us.’”
“When he came back as king, he called in the servants he’d given the money to. He wanted to find out what they’d earned.”
“The first one came in and said, ‘Sir, your mina earned ten more.’”
“The king said, ‘Well done, good servant! You were faithful with a little, so now you’re in charge of ten cities.’”
“The second came in and said, ‘Sir, your mina earned five more.’”
“The king told him, ‘You’re in charge of five cities.’”
“Another servant came in and said, ‘Sir, here’s your mina. I kept it wrapped up in a cloth,”
“‘because I was scared of you. You’re a tough man: you take what you didn’t put down and harvest what you didn’t plant.’”
“The king said, ‘I’ll judge you by your own words, you wicked servant! You knew I was tough, taking what I didn’t put down and harvesting what I didn’t plant.”
“‘So why didn’t you put my money in the bank? Then when I came back, I could’ve collected it with interest.’”
“He told the people standing there, ‘Take that mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten.’”
“They said, ‘Sir, he already has ten minas!’”
“‘I’m telling you, everyone who has will get more. But whoever has nothing—even what they have will be taken away.”
“‘And bring my enemies here—the ones who didn’t want me ruling over them—and kill them in front of me.’”
After telling them this, Jesus went on ahead, heading up to Jerusalem.
When he came near Bethphage and Bethany, by the hill called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples.
He said, “Go to the village over there. As you enter, you’ll find a young donkey tied up, one nobody has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.”
“If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell them, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
The two disciples went and found it just as Jesus had told them.
As they were untying the donkey, its owners asked, “Why are you untying it?”
They said, “The Lord needs it.”
They brought it to Jesus, threw their cloaks over the donkey, and sat Jesus on it.
As he rode along, people spread their cloaks on the road.
When he was coming down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples started celebrating and praising God loudly for all the miracles they’d seen. 🙌
They shouted, “Blessed is the King who comes in the Lord’s name! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
Some Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, tell your disciples to stop!”
He answered, “I’m telling you, if they went quiet, the stones would start shouting.”
When Jesus came closer and saw the city, he wept over it.
He said, “If only you’d understood today what could bring you peace! But now it’s hidden from your eyes.”
“The days are coming when your enemies will build a barricade around you. They’ll surround you, close in from every side,”
“and crush you and your children to the ground. They won’t leave one stone on top of another, because you didn’t recognize the time God came to you.”
Jesus entered the temple and began driving out the people buying and selling there.
He said, “The Scriptures say, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you’ve turned it into a ‘hideout for robbers’!”
Jesus taught in the temple every day. The chief priests, the law teachers, and the leaders of the people were looking for a way to kill him.
But they couldn’t find a way to do it, because all the people were hanging on every word he said.
One day, while Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and sharing the Good News, the priests, law teachers, and elders walked up.
They challenged him: “Tell us, what gives you the right to do this? Who gave you that authority?”
He answered, “I’ve got a question for you too. Tell me this:”
“Was John’s baptism from heaven, or was it just from people?”
They talked it over: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him?’”
“But if we say, ‘From people,’ the crowd will stone us—they’re convinced John was a prophet.”
So they answered, “We don’t know where it came from.”
Jesus said, “Then I’m not telling you who gave me authority to do these things either.”
Then he told the people this story: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it to some farmers, and went away to another country for a long time.”
“When harvest time came, he sent a servant to collect his share of the grapes. But the farmers beat him and sent him off with nothing.”
“The owner sent another servant, but they beat him too, treated him terribly, and sent him off empty-handed.”
“He sent a third servant. They wounded him too and threw him out.”
“The vineyard owner thought, ‘What now? I’ll send my beloved son. Maybe they’ll respect him when they see him.’”
“But when the farmers saw the son, they talked it over: ‘This is the heir! Let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’”
“So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What do you think the vineyard owner will do to them now?”
“He’ll come and destroy those farmers, then hand the vineyard to others.” When the people heard that, they said, “No way—may that never happen!”
Jesus looked right at them and said, “Then what does this Scripture mean: ‘The stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone’?”
“Everyone who trips over that stone will be shattered, and whoever it falls on will be crushed to dust.”
The chief priests and law teachers wanted to grab Jesus right then, but they were scared of the crowd. They knew his story was aimed at them.
They kept watching him and sent spies pretending to be good people. They wanted to catch him saying something they could use to hand him over to the governor’s power.
They asked, “Teacher, we know you speak and teach what’s right. You don’t play favorites; you truly teach God’s way.”
“So, is it allowed for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
Jesus saw through their setup and said, “Why are you testing me?”
“Show me a denarius. Whose face and name are stamped on it?” They answered, “Caesar’s.”
He said, “Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give God what belongs to God.”
They couldn’t trap him in front of the people. His answer amazed them, and they went quiet.
Some Sadducees came over—the group that says there’s no resurrection.
They asked him, “Teacher, Moses wrote that if a man’s brother dies, leaves a wife but no children, the brother should marry her and raise children for his brother.”
“There were seven brothers. The first married a woman, then died without children.”
“The second married her, then he died without children too.”
“Then the third married her. Same story with all seven: no children, and they all died.”
“Later, the woman died too.”
“So when the dead rise, whose wife will she be? All seven were married to her.”
Jesus said, “People in this age marry and are given in marriage.”
“But the people who are considered worthy of the coming age and rising from the dead won’t marry or be given in marriage.”
“They can’t die anymore. They’re like the angels and are God’s children, raised to new life.”
“Even Moses showed that the dead are raised at the burning bush, when he called the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’”
“God isn’t God of the dead, but of the living. To him, they’re all alive.”
Some law teachers replied, “Teacher, well said.”
After that, nobody dared ask him another question.
Then Jesus asked them, “Why do people say the Messiah is David’s son?”
“David himself says in the Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand,””
“‘until I put your enemies under your feet.’”
“So David calls him Lord. How, then, can he be David’s son?”
While everyone was listening, Jesus said to his disciples:
“Watch out for those law teachers. They love strutting around in long robes, soaking up greetings in the marketplaces, and claiming the best seats in the synagogues and at feasts.”
“They rob widows of their homes, then put on a show with long prayers. They’ll face a harsher judgment.”
Jesus looked up and saw the rich folks putting their gifts into the temple offering box.
He also saw a poor widow drop in two tiny coins.
He said, “I’m telling you the truth: this poor widow gave more than all of them put together.”
“They gave gifts from what they had plenty of, but she gave from her need—everything she had to live on.”
Some people were talking about the temple: its beautiful stonework and all the gifts decorating it. Jesus said,
“The day is coming when every one of these things you’re looking at will be torn down. Not one stone will stay on top of another.”
They asked him, “Teacher, when will this happen? What sign will show that it’s about to go down?”
He said, “Watch out—don’t let anyone play you. Many will come using my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is here!’ Don’t follow them.”
“When you hear about wars and uprisings, don’t panic. These things have to happen first, but the end won’t come right away.”
Then he told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.”
“There will be major earthquakes, famines, and diseases in different places. Terrifying things will happen, and there’ll be huge signs in the sky.”
“But before all that, people will arrest you and persecute you. They’ll hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and bring you before kings and governors because you follow me.”
“That will become your chance to testify about me.”
“So settle this in your heart: don’t rehearse your defense ahead of time.”
“I’ll give you words and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to argue with or shut down.”
“Even your parents, siblings, relatives, and friends will hand you over. Some of you will be put to death.”
“Everyone will hate you because you bear my name.”
“But not one hair on your head will be lost.”
“Stand firm, and you’ll gain your life.”
“When you see armies surrounding Jerusalem, know that its destruction is near.”
“Then let the people in Judea run to the mountains. Those inside Jerusalem should get out, and those out in the countryside shouldn’t go into the city.”
“These are days of justice, when everything written will be fulfilled.”
“How awful it will be for pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days! The land will face terrible distress, and this people will face judgment.”
“They’ll be killed by the sword and taken captive to every nation. Gentiles will trample Jerusalem until their time is complete.”
“There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars. On earth, nations will be terrified and confused by the roaring sea and its waves.”
“People will faint from fear, dreading what’s coming over the world, because the powers of the heavens will be shaken.”
“Then they’ll see the Son of Man coming in a cloud, with power and great glory.”
“When these things start happening, stand up and lift your heads—your rescue is getting close.”
Then Jesus told them a story: “Look at the fig tree and all the other trees.”
“When they start budding, you can see for yourselves that summer is close.”
“Same thing here: when you see these events happening, know God’s Kingdom is close.”
“I’m telling you the truth: this generation won’t pass away before all these things happen.”
“Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.”
“So watch yourselves. Don’t let partying, getting drunk, or everyday worries weigh your hearts down, or that day will catch you off guard.”
“It’ll come like a trap for everyone living across the whole earth.”
“Stay alert and pray all the time, so you’ll have strength to get through everything that’s coming and stand before the Son of Man.”
Every day Jesus taught in the temple. Every night he went out and stayed on the mountain called Olivet.
All the people came early each morning to hear him in the temple.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread, also called Passover, was coming up.
The chief priests and law teachers were looking for a way to kill Jesus, but they were scared of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, the one also called Iscariot, who was one of the twelve.
Judas went and talked with the chief priests and temple guards about how to hand Jesus over.
They were pleased and agreed to pay him.
Judas said yes, then started looking for a chance to hand Jesus over when the crowd wasn’t around.
The day came when the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John: “Go get the Passover meal ready for us so we can eat.”
They asked, “Where do you want us to set it up?”
He said, “When you get into the city, a man carrying a water jar will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters.”
“Tell the owner, ‘The Teacher asks, “Where’s the guest room where I can eat the Passover with my disciples?”’”
“He’ll show you a large upstairs room, already set up. Get things ready there.”
They went and found everything just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When the time came, Jesus sat down with the twelve apostles.
He told them, “I’ve been looking forward so deeply to eating this Passover with you before I suffer,”
“because I’m telling you, I won’t eat it again until it’s fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
He took a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and share it among yourselves,”
“because I’m telling you, I won’t drink from the vine again until God’s Kingdom comes.”
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them: “This is my body, given for you. Keep doing this to remember me.”
After supper, he took the cup too and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.”
“But look—the hand of the one betraying me is right here at the table.”
“The Son of Man is going where God has determined, but how terrible for the one who betrays him!”
They started asking each other which one of them would do this.
Then they started arguing about which of them was the greatest.
Jesus told them, “The kings of the nations boss people around, and the rulers like being called ‘benefactors.’”
“That’s not how it should be with you. The greatest among you should become like the youngest, and the leader should serve.”
“Who’s greater: the one sitting at the table or the one serving? Isn’t it the one at the table? But I’m here among you as the one who serves.”
“You’re the ones who stayed with me through my trials.”
“I’m giving you a kingdom, just as my Father gave one to me,”
“so you can eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You’ll sit on thrones and judge Israel’s twelve tribes.”
The Lord said, “Simon, Simon, listen: Satan demanded to sift all of you like wheat,”
“but I prayed for you, Simon, so your faith wouldn’t fail. When you come back, strengthen your brothers.”
Peter said, “Lord, I’m ready to go with you to prison—even to death!”
Jesus said, “Peter, I’m telling you, before the rooster crows today, you’ll deny three times that you know me.”
He asked them, “When I sent you out without a wallet, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “Nothing.”
Then he said, “But now, if you have a wallet, take it, and take a bag too. If you don’t have a sword, sell your coat and buy one.”
“I’m telling you, this Scripture still has to come true in me: ‘He was counted among the lawless.’ What concerns me is reaching its fulfillment.”
They said, “Lord, look—we have two swords.” He told them, “That’s enough.”
Jesus went out to the Mount of Olives, as he usually did, and his disciples followed him.
When they got there, he told them, “Pray that you don’t give in to temptation.”
He went about a stone’s throw away, knelt down, and prayed:
“Father, if you’re willing, take this cup away from me. Still, let your will happen, not mine.”
An angel from heaven appeared and strengthened him.
In deep anguish, Jesus prayed even harder. His sweat fell to the ground like big drops of blood.
When he got up from praying, he went back to the disciples and found them asleep from grief.
He said, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray so you don’t give in to temptation.”
While he was still speaking, a crowd showed up, led by Judas, one of the twelve. Judas came close to Jesus to kiss him.
Jesus said, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When the disciples around Jesus saw what was coming, they asked, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?”
One of them struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus said, “That’s enough of this.” He touched the man’s ear and healed him.
Jesus said to the chief priests, temple guards, and elders who came for him, “Did you come out here after me like I’m a robber, carrying swords and clubs?”
“I was with you in the temple every day, and you never laid a hand on me. But this is your hour—the hour when darkness gets its way.”
They arrested Jesus and led him to the high priest’s house. Peter followed from a distance.
They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together. Peter sat with them.
A servant girl saw Peter sitting by the fire. She stared at him and said, “This man was with Jesus too.”
Peter denied it: “Woman, I don’t know him.”
A little later, someone else saw Peter and said, “You’re one of them too!” Peter answered, “Man, I’m not!”
About an hour later, another person insisted, “For sure, this man was with Jesus. He’s a Galilean!”
Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you’re talking about!” Right then, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Peter remembered what the Lord had told him: “Before the rooster crows, you’ll deny me three times.”
Peter went outside and cried bitterly. 😢
The men guarding Jesus mocked him and beat him.
They blindfolded him, hit him in the face, and said, “Come on, prophet—who hit you?”
They kept insulting him and saying all kinds of things against him.
When morning came, the elders of the people gathered—the chief priests and law teachers too. They brought Jesus before their council and said:
“If you’re the Messiah, tell us.” He answered, “If I tell you, you won’t believe me.”
“And if I ask you a question, you won’t answer or let me go.”
“From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of God’s power.”
They all asked, “So are you the Son of God?” He said, “You say I am.”
They said, “Why do we need more witnesses? We heard it ourselves from his own mouth!”
The whole group got up and brought Jesus to Pilate.
They began accusing him: “We caught this man turning the nation upside down, telling people not to pay Caesar’s taxes, and claiming he’s the Messiah—a king.”
Pilate asked Jesus, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You said it.”
Pilate told the chief priests and the crowd, “I find no reason to charge this man.”
But they kept pushing: “He’s stirring up the people, teaching all through Judea, from Galilee right down here!”
When Pilate heard them mention Galilee, he asked if Jesus was a Galilean.
When he learned Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at the time.
Herod was thrilled to see Jesus. He’d wanted to meet him for a long time after hearing all the stories, and hoped to see him do a miracle.
Herod questioned Jesus again and again, but Jesus didn’t answer.
The chief priests and law teachers stood there, fiercely accusing him.
Herod and his soldiers mocked and humiliated Jesus. They dressed him in fancy clothes and sent him back to Pilate.
That very day, Herod and Pilate became friends. Before this, they’d been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the leaders, and the people.
He said, “You brought this man to me, saying he was turning the people against you. I questioned him right here in front of you, and I found no basis for your charges.”
“Herod didn’t find anything either—I sent you to him. Jesus hasn’t done anything deserving death.”
“So I’ll have him beaten and then release him.”
At the festival, Pilate was supposed to release one prisoner to the people.
But they all shouted together, “Get rid of this man! Release Barabbas to us!”
Barabbas had been thrown in prison for starting a revolt in the city and committing murder.
Pilate spoke to them again, because he wanted to release Jesus.
But they shouted, “Crucify him! Crucify him!”
Pilate asked them a third time, “Why? What evil has he done? I found no crime deserving death. I’ll have him beaten and release him.”
But they kept shouting, louder and louder, demanding that Jesus be crucified. Their voices—and the chief priests’ voices—won out.
Pilate ruled that their demand should be carried out.
He released the man they had asked for, the one jailed for revolt and murder. But he handed Jesus over to their will.
As they led Jesus away, they grabbed Simon from Cyrene, who was coming in from the countryside, and put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A huge crowd followed Jesus, including women who were mourning and crying for him.
Jesus turned to them and said, “Women of Jerusalem, don’t cry for me. Cry for yourselves and your children.”
“The days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the women who never had children, the wombs that never carried a baby, and the breasts that never nursed.’”
“Then they’ll beg the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and the hills, ‘Cover us!’”
“If this is what they do while the tree is green, what will happen when it’s dry?”
Two other men, both criminals, were being led out with Jesus to be executed.
When they reached the place called The Skull, they crucified Jesus there with the criminals—one on his right, the other on his left.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them; they don’t know what they’re doing.” Then the soldiers divided his clothes and rolled dice for them.
The people stood watching. The leaders sneered too: “He saved others! If he’s God’s Messiah, the Chosen One, let him save himself!”
The soldiers mocked him too. They came up and offered him sour wine.
They said, “If you’re the King of the Jews, save yourself!”
An inscription was placed above him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
One of the criminals hanging there insulted Jesus: “Aren’t you the Messiah? Save yourself—and us!”
But the other criminal corrected him: “Don’t you fear God? You’re facing the same sentence.”
“We’re getting what we deserve for what we did, but this man hasn’t done anything wrong.”
Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
Jesus told him, “I’m telling you the truth: today you’ll be with me in Paradise.”
It was about noon, and darkness covered the whole land until three in the afternoon.
The sun went dark, and the temple curtain split down the middle.
Jesus shouted loudly, “Father, I place my spirit in your hands!” After saying this, he died.
When the Roman officer saw what had happened, he praised God and said, “This man really was righteous.”
The crowds that had gathered to watch saw what happened, then went home beating their chests in grief.
Everyone who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed him from Galilee, stood at a distance and watched.
There was a man named Joseph, a member of the council. He was a good and righteous man.
He had not agreed with the council’s plan or what they had done. He was from Arimathea, a Judean town, and he was waiting for God’s Kingdom.
Joseph went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
He took the body down, wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a tomb cut into rock, where nobody had ever been buried.
It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph. They saw the tomb and how Jesus’ body was laid there.
Then they went back and prepared spices and perfumes. On the Sabbath, they rested, as the commandment required.
On the first day of the week, just before sunrise, the women came to the tomb with the spices they’d prepared.
They found the stone rolled away from the entrance.
They went inside, but the Lord Jesus’ body wasn’t there.
While they were trying to figure out what happened, two men suddenly stood beside them in dazzling clothes.
The women were terrified and bowed their faces to the ground. The men said, “Why are you looking for the living among the dead?”
“He’s not here. He’s risen! Remember what he told you back in Galilee:”
“‘The Son of Man has to be handed over to sinful people, crucified, and rise again on the third day’?”
Then they remembered what Jesus had said.
They returned from the tomb and told all this to the eleven and everyone else.
The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James. The other women with them told the apostles too.
But the apostles thought it was nonsense, and they didn’t believe the women.
Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and saw the linen cloths by themselves. Then he went home, wondering what on earth had happened.
That same day, two of them were walking to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
They were talking together about everything that had happened.
As they talked it over, Jesus himself came up and walked with them.
But somehow they weren’t able to recognize him.
He asked them, “What are you two talking about as you walk? You look pretty down.”
One of them, Cleopas, answered, “Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who hasn’t heard what’s been happening these last few days?”
He asked, “What happened?” They said, “It’s about Jesus from Nazareth. He was a prophet, powerful in what he said and did before God and all the people.”
“The chief priests and our leaders handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they crucified him.”
“We had hoped he was the one who would rescue Israel. And on top of that, today’s the third day since it all happened.”
“Some women from our group really shook us up. They went to the tomb early this morning,”
“but couldn’t find his body. They came back saying they’d seen angels in a vision, and the angels said Jesus was alive.”
“Some of us went to the tomb too. It was just like the women said, but they didn’t see Jesus.”
Jesus said, “You’re missing the point and taking forever to believe everything the prophets said!”
“Didn’t the Messiah have to suffer these things before entering his glory?”
Then, starting with Moses and going through all the prophets, he explained what all the Scriptures said about himself.
They came near the village they were heading to, and Jesus acted like he was going farther.
But they urged him, “Stay with us. It’s almost evening; the day’s nearly done.” So he went in to stay with them.
When he sat down at the table, he took the bread and gave thanks. Then he broke it and passed it to them.
Suddenly their eyes opened, and they recognized him. Then he vanished from their sight.
They said to each other, “Weren’t our hearts burning inside us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
They got up right then and went back to Jerusalem. They found the eleven gathered with the others,
who said, “It’s true! The Lord has risen and appeared to Simon!”
Then the two told what happened on the road and how they recognized Jesus when he broke the bread.
While they were talking about all this, Jesus himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
They were terrified and scared out of their minds, thinking they were seeing a spirit.
He said, “Why are you so shaken? Why are doubts popping up in your hearts?”
“Look at my hands and feet—it’s really me. Touch me and see. A spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones like you can see I have.”
After saying this, he showed them his hands and feet.
They still couldn’t believe it because they were so amazed and joyful. Jesus asked, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave him a piece of cooked fish and some honeycomb.
He took it and ate it in front of them.
Then he said, “This is what I told you while I was still with you: everything written about me in Moses’ Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms has to come true.”
Then he opened their minds so they could understand the Scriptures.
He told them, “This is what’s written: the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,”
“and repentance and forgiveness of sins must be announced in his name to every nation, starting in Jerusalem.”
“You are witnesses of all this.”
“Listen, I’m sending you what my Father promised. Stay in Jerusalem until you’re clothed with power from above.”
Jesus led them out toward Bethany. He raised his hands and blessed them.
While he was blessing them, he left them and was carried up into heaven.
They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem full of joy.
They stayed in the temple all the time, praising and blessing God. Amen. 🙌
